Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Replay gameplay helpers

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

These are engine-independent operations on frame-owned values. Games choose the system order and pass immutable rules; helpers do not select authority or access scene nodes. Units are per simulation tick unless specified otherwise.

  • Body2/move: axis-separated movement against authored static AABBs.
  • Motion2/momentum_step: velocity approaches a target, then position integrates and clamps to bounds. roll_step applies friction, speed cap and wall restitution from Roll_Law2. soft_contact separates half the overlap and applies a bounded motion-directed dribble nudge. These are a defined kinematic subset, not a general rigid-body solver or a proof of cross-platform determinism.
  • Cooldown: frame-owned countdown with tick/ready/arm operations and cooldown_try for admission that starts the clock only when ready.
  • Gun_State: magazine, reload and deterministic jam/clear transitions; the caller owns cadence and shot effects.
  • Carom2 and beam queries: value-owned bouncing ordnance and the closed-segment judge used by the Scrapyard lance/mender.
  • Effect and Telegraph: bounded stack/duration state and explicit wind-up/landing clocks; games supply reactions, attribution and payloads.
  • Director and Channel: paced waves with spawn backpressure and validated tick-owned holds such as revives.
  • Inventory, damage/reach and navigation helpers support the Cavecrawl model.
  • Ray/AABB/circle queries, life-aware hurtbox interpolation and semantic spawn keys support Quickdraw.

Speedball is the motion/contact example. Its movement, ball integration and contacts execute identically in native tests, the server and full-world client prediction. Godot presentation reads copies.
